content.comment_body: At our site we have three groups of interconnected [product_name] devices. The groups are: 1. Three [product_name] units plus one [product_name] operator device connected together; 2. Two [product_name] units networked together; 3. Four [product_name] units linked with two [product_name] operator devices. All devices share the same physical network. I am hoping to link all these groups to a single [product_name] communications module to send fault alert messages from all groups. The manual mentions: "You can configure static/dynamic connections as required, for instance, n static and 16-n dynamic connections. [product_name] supports up to eight static connections." Despite this, there isn't clear guidance in the documentation about configuring static versus dynamic connections. My aim is to keep static connections within each group and have dynamic connections from each group to the communications module. Any advice would be appreciated.
The communications module can connect to only one [product_name] device.

Thanks for the confirmation. So it is possible for one [product_name] in each system to establish a dynamic connection with a central [product_name] attached to the communications module? Would this solve my requirement? Your diagram clarifies how static and dynamic connection points function. Are there any limitations with dynamic connections? Could these be used for sending occasional alert messages?
Sorry, I have no further insights on this matter. I only know what’s described in the manual.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to connect multiple [product_name] devices and [product_name] operator units in a combined static/dynamic network with a [product_name] communications module for centralized messaging. There is uncertainty regarding the network's technical limitations, how to properly set up static and dynamic links, and any restrictions on dynamic messaging connections, especially for intermittent alerts. The current documentation appears to lack detailed explanations for dynamic configuration and potential connection constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking detailed documentation and proven approaches for enabling several [product_name] systems to link dynamically to a central communications module for alert distribution. They want clarity about connection restrictions, practical advice for dynamic connection setup, and assurance that dynamic connections are appropriate for sending infrequent notifications.
